h: What to pack and how to plan the splash
p: A good day at a waterpark starts with a good bag. Pack swimwear, a towel each, flip-flops or pool shoes for walking around, a bottle of water and a waterproof pouch for your phone if you plan to take it near the water. Goggles are handy for anyone who hates getting splashed in the eyes, and a change of warm clothes for afterwards is a must when you're heading back out into the Blackpool breeze.

Lockers make life much easier. Grab one early so you're not carrying valuables around, and make sure everyone in your group knows where it is. It's a big place, so agreeing a meeting point is a sensible move if older kids want to go off on the bigger slides on their own.

How long to allow? Most families will want to make a good few hours of it, so book a session that gives you enough time to get changed, try the slides and still have a sit-down break. Children tend to want just one more go on their favourites, so building in extra time saves arguments at the end.
Food and drink are available inside, so you can refuel without getting dressed again. Little ones will need breaks in the warm, especially after a busy morning.

Afterwards, step back out onto the promenade and you're in the heart of Blackpool's south end. Pleasure Beach is right next door for rides, South Pier is close by and a tram ride north along the seafront takes you to the Tower, the Golden Mile and Central Pier. Grab fish and chips and finish the day with a walk along the sands.
